content.title: What about the harm Christians have done?
content.summary: Tell the truth about sin. Christ's name must never shield wrongdoing.

answer.text: Sin in the church must be named and confronted, not excused because the offender claims Christian faith. Scripture condemns hypocrisy and requires accountability. Christ is sinless; his followers are not. That distinction calls the church to repentance rather than giving it an escape from responsibility.

reasoning.text: A Christian label does not establish genuine faith or faithful conduct.
The church is responsible to address serious wrongdoing within it.
Repentance produces fruit; it is more than a demand that others stop discussing the harm.

conclusion.text: We defend the truth of Christ by telling the truth about evil and pursuing faithful accountability, not by protecting a reputation at any cost.

sections.text: Ask what happened and resist answering a particular person's pain with a general slogan. Love listens and grieves. Fairness also requires care with testimony; neither reflexive denial nor an unsupported accusation serves the truth.
sections.title: Listen before defending an institution

sections.text: Southern Baptists have their own record to face. The Southern Baptist Convention was founded in 1845, when Baptists in the South separated from Baptists in the North over slavery. Its 1995 resolution, adopted at its 150th anniversary meeting, acknowledged the role slavery played in its formation, repudiated historic acts of evil such as slavery, and apologised to all African-Americans for condoning and perpetuating individual and systemic racism in its members' lifetime. On 22 May 2022 an independent investigation by Guidepost Solutions, which the Convention's messengers had voted for in 2021, reported that for years a few senior Executive Committee leaders and outside lawyers had been focused on avoiding legal liability, so that survivors who reported abuse were often ignored or disbelieved. It also found that since 2007 a staff member had kept a list of accused ministers, the latest version holding 703 names, with no sign that anyone acted to keep them out of ministry. Telling this truth is part of repentance, not an attack on the gospel.
sections.title: Our own house

sections.text: Church discipline seeks repentance and restoration while taking sin seriously. It is not a substitute for civil responsibility. Abuse, or a reasonable suspicion of it, is reported to the police and the civil authorities, and to child-protection services when a child is involved; a church never handles it privately. Jesus' steps of going to a brother privately, then with witnesses, then to the church concern a fellow believer's sin against you; they never require a victim to confront an abuser alone or keep a crime from the authorities. Christian submission to governing authorities does not allow a church to treat itself as beyond accountability.
sections.title: Repentance and accountability

content.objection: Why should I trust a faith whose followers behave like that?

reply.text: The offence should not be minimised. Jesus himself exposes religious hypocrisy. His life and gospel deserve examination on their own truth, while the church must answer to the standards it professes.

limit.text: Forgiveness must not be used as permission to continue harming people or avoid the fruits of repentance. This study supplies biblical principles, not a determination of the facts in an individual case.

prompt.text: What happened, and what would it mean for Christians to take that wrong seriously?
